title: FlowTrace happy path: agent-authored artifact to source navigation

node-1.label: Agent researches the code and writes a FlowTrace artifact
node-1.summary: The happy path starts with the coding agent reading the repository and authoring the final .flow.json. The CLI is not responsible for LLM reasoning; it validates and previews the artifact after the agent writes it.

node-2.label: Artifact follows the FlowTrace schema
node-2.summary: A FlowTrace file contains a schema version, title, root node id, and a map of nodes. Each node can include file, line, anchor, symbol, summary, children, and branches.

node-3.label: User or agent runs flowtrace validate
node-3.summary: The CLI dispatches the validate command, which loads the artifact and checks it against the repository root before the user opens it in Neovim.

node-4.label: ValidateFlow checks files, lines, and references
node-4.summary: Validation ensures required fields exist, every referenced file is real, line numbers are in range, resolution values are known, and children/branches point at real node ids.

node-5.label: flowtrace print previews the tree in the terminal
node-5.summary: The print command renders the root, children, and branches as a terminal tree so the agent can catch shape issues before handing the artifact to the user.

node-6.label: User opens the artifact with :FlowTraceOpen
node-6.summary: The Neovim plugin registers :FlowTraceOpen and forwards the selected .flow.json path into the Lua module.

node-7.label: M.open loads JSON and creates the FlowTrace pane
node-7.summary: M.open stores the source window, parses the artifact, opens the FlowTrace buffer, installs keymaps, and calls redraw to render the tree.

node-8.label: parser.load decodes and sanity-checks the artifact
node-8.summary: The parser reads the JSON file with vim.fn.readfile, decodes it with vim.json.decode, and verifies the root and nodes fields exist.

node-9.label: tree.render turns nodes into visible rows
node-9.summary: Rendering creates the title/help rows, recursively flattens the node graph, records a row-to-node index, and returns highlight spans for labels, types, files, and summaries.

node-10.label: Pressing Enter jumps to the real source location
node-10.summary: The jump action finds the current tree row, opens the node file in a code window, resolves anchor then symbol then line, and moves the cursor to the source location.
